title: The Bark Mask
text: A face has grown into the bark of an old oak, eyes half lidded, mouth knotted shut. It turns in the wood with a creak to follow you as you pass. It will let the most unseeing of you borrow its eyes, it whispers, for a little while.

options.label: The poorest eye borrows the oak's eyes, eager to see what the wood sees.

outcomes.text: Through the oak's eyes they see every root, snare and path in the wood. They give the eyes back reluctantly.
They see what the wood sees. It is hungry, and it has been watching all of you for a long time.

options.label: The strongest cuts the face out of the tree, before it whispers any more.

outcomes.text: Every tree in the wood screams at once. The mask is fine work with its eyes shut, yet you feel them on you.

options.label: Nod to it, as to a neighbour, and pass on your way.

outcomes.text: The face creaks into something like a smile. Ahead, the branches part a little.
